[[Las Vegas management Vault]] |occupation =Congresswoman |affiliation =[[United States Congress|U.S. House of Representatives]] |role =Mainframe |rank = |TV actor =[[Martha Kelly]] }} {{Quotation|Fighting the good fight is mostly a series of humiliations.}} '''Diane Welch''' is a member of the [[United States Congress]] before the [[Great War]] who appears in the [[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'' TV series]]. ==Background== Welch served as a U.S. representative from the congressional district encompassing [[Glendale]], [[California]] in the 2070s. She was seemingly an unpopular elected official, however, being the only incumbent member of Congress who refused all corporate donors due to her objections to the influence of corporations such as [[Vault-Tec Corporation|Vault-Tec]] in the [[United States government]]. ==''Fallout'' TV series== ===[[The Profligate]]=== Representative Welch appears at the event organized by the [[American Veteran Entertainment Alliance]] and [[Veterans of Foreign Wars of the United States]] to honor [[United States Marine Corps|Marine]] [[Charles Whiteknife|Corporal Charles Whiteknife]]. Her uncharismatic opening speech is ridiculed by the audience as she drops her packet of notes and stumbles to retrieve them. Later on, Whiteknife takes the podium after being introduced by her as he entertains the audience by recalling a war story where he helped save the life of his friend and fellow Marine, [[The Ghoul|Cooper Howard]]. At the end of his speech about doing one's duty and protecting their loved ones, Welch awards him with a commemorative lighter that he would later give to Cooper instead. ===[[The Wrangler]]=== [[File:Welch Las Vegas.jpeg|thumb|279x279px|Welch protesting against the presence of corporate leaders in Vegas, before being thrown out by MP officers]] During the summit meeting between the captains of industry in [[New Vegas|Las Vegas]], [[Nevada]], Welch joined with ongoing protests and managed to get inside the [[Lucky 38]] host venue to protest directly before ultimately being escorted out and thrown to the sidewalk by [[Military Police officer|MPs]]. She is helped up by a recently arrived Cooper, remarking that her efforts of "fighting the good fight" only serve to humiliate her more, until she notices who helped her up. Welch is stunned that a high-profile character like Cooper would be kind to her, as he tells her to keep up her opposition before going to join his wife [[Barb Howard|Barb]]. {{clear}} ===[[The Handoff]]=== After Cooper successfully acquired the [[Cold fusion|cold fusion diode]] with Barb's blessing, he debates how to keep it out of the hands of House and Vault-Tec. This leads him to seek out Welch, firstly by paying the bail to get her out of jail after she continued her protests and was arrested, then inviting her to the [[Atomic Wrangler Casino]]. Cooper sympathizes with what he sees as her nature as a good person in opposing the corporations, though he lightly scolds her for her seeming lack of energy in her campaign including what she demonstrated at the veteran's hall before. She tries to counter by pointing out his spokesmanship with Vault-Tec, but he takes it in stride and lays out the essentials of what he has learned in that time, primarily that Vault-Tec plans to trade the infinite energy of cold fusion to [[Robert House]] in exchange for getting the weaponry they need to start nuclear war while ensuring theirs is the only power left. Cooper asks what she might do if he could ensure the deal fell through and got cold fusion into her hands, to which Welch says she would give it away to the public and make it work for the good of the American people, not just the corporations. Cooper however remains skeptical of what could happen and Welch agrees that it is not a foolproof plan. But then she reveals something else: an earlier landing of an unmarked government aircraft [[Camp McCarran|McCarran Airport]], carrying the [[Last President of the United States|president of the United States]]. Cooper asks stunningly if she can really arrange a meeting between him and the president, which she confirms, saying they could functionally end the [[Resource Wars]] in one night. Later at night, as Cooper and Barb walk the streets of Las Vegas, they see a discreet vehicle pull up ahead of them which Cooper then enters to sit beside Welch and across from the president himself. Before the congresswoman, he hands over the cold fusion diode. 219 years after this event, as [[Lucy MacLean]] is exploring the basement containing the mainframe for the [[brain-computer interface chip]]s being used by her father [[Hank MacLean]] to create an army of mind-controlled Vault-Tec staff, she enters the room where the mainframe is stored to discover that it is actually the severed head of Diane Welch, hooked up to a neutral control helmet much like the one used by House that broadcasts her brain patterns into the minds of every chipped victim once they are induced with amnesia, turning them into cheerful, obedient corporate drones. ===[[The Strip]]=== After Lucy finds Welch in the mainframe room, Welch begs Lucy to kill her. After some hesitation, Lucy complies, smashing her head in and putting an end to her life. ==Personality== Though she occupies a high station as an elected government official, Diane Welch's public profile is one dominated by a complete lack of charisma, including giving speeches with an unenthusiastic monotone delivery. In spite of her reputation, Welch proves herself to have an incorruptible morality, even as it leaves her a minority in the increasingly corporatist environment within the pre-War U.S. government to which she stands as the sole member of Congress that opposes corporate influence, as she is willing to make a physical stand against what she opposes even when it results in public humiliation and arrest by law enforcement. According to [[Hank MacLean]], Welch had a [[Wikipedia:Myers–Briggs Type Indicator|Myers-Briggs personality type]] of ISTP (introverted, observant, thinking, and prospecting), which was reportedly the "gold standard" for [[Vault-Tec Corporation]] personnel. Hank said this made her an ideal personality to add to the [[brain-computer interface chip]] mainframe, with traits such as being "well-meaning, sweet, [and] non-threatening."{{FOTV|2|8}} ==Notes== {{Note|(Note)}} Welch is never given a definitive age in the series. In the real world, members of the U.S. House of Representatives must be at least 25 years old to take office, and it is visually apparent Welch is older than this. With the Great War falling in [[Timeline (2050-2099)#2077|2077]], by the time of Welch's appearance in [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2296|2296]], 244+ is a bare minimum age range for how old she must be. ==Appearances== Representative Diane Welch appears only {{In|FOTV}}. {{FOTV appearances|11=203|13=205|15=207|16=208}} ==Gallery== Congresswoman Welch The Wrangler.png|In "[[The Wrangler]]" FTV S2E7 Still 196.png|Mainframe room, "[[The Strip]]" ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox characters FOTV}} {{Navbox cyborgs}} [[Category:Fallout TV series human characters]] [[Category:Pre-War politicians]] [[ru:Дайан Уэлч]]
